# Scope

This report compares schizophrenia burden in China and the United States from
1990 through 2023, separately for females and males. Outcomes are incidence,
prevalence, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), reported as all-age
numbers and age-standardized rates. The demographic decomposition uses official
GBD 2023 population estimates and 20 mutually exclusive five-year age groups
from 0-4 years through 95+ years.

The burden and population inputs have retained export metadata and SHA-256
fingerprints. The source exports contain 2,720 exact zero Number/Rate cells.
These values were preserved and audited; they were not interpreted as proof of
biological absence.

# Methods

Annual age-standardized rates were summarized using an open Python
BIC-selected segmented log-linear model allowing zero to two breakpoints.
Breakpoint locations, segment changes, and average annual percentage changes
are descriptive point estimates. A feasible-GLS AR(1) sensitivity assesses
serial correlation. Continuous changes are primary; the +/-0.05% per year
practical-stability label and its +/-0.02% and +/-0.10% sensitivities are
reporting rules rather than equivalence tests.

Changes in reconstructed all-age quantities were decomposed into population
size, age structure, and age-specific rate components by averaging over all six
factor-replacement orders (a Shapley decomposition). Endpoint, annual-chain,
five-year-chain, collapsed-age, and positive-supported-age sensitivities assess
path and aggregation dependence.

The secondary age-period-cohort analysis is custom and descriptive. It reports
a global period slope, separately fitted age-specific slopes, an age rate-ratio
curve, and period- and cohort-curvature rate ratios for ages 10-14 through
65-69 years. Incidence is the principal secondary outcome; prevalence and DALY
rate surfaces are exploratory. No equivalence to conventional NCI APC
estimable functions is claimed.

# Principal findings

Point estimates of incident cases, prevalent cases, and DALYs increased from
1990 to 2023 in every country-sex stratum. DALY age-standardized rates in China
changed from 175.3 to 177.6 per 100,000 among females and from 207.2 to 209.1
among males. Corresponding United States rates changed from 269.5 to 247.9
among females and from 281.2 to 270.2 among males.

Under the stated descriptive stability band, Chinese segmented AAPCs were
practically stable and United States AAPCs were negative. The AR(1) sensitivity
preserved the practical trajectory label in all 12 country-sex-outcome panels,
preserved breakpoint count in 11 panels, and changed AAPC by no more than 0.009
percentage points per year.

Population-size change was positive in all 12 decompositions. Age-structure and
age-specific-rate components varied by country, sex, and outcome. Annual- and
five-year-chain allocations differed from endpoint allocations by at most 7.9%
of total change. Restricting incidence to positive-valued ages 10-79 preserved
all component signs, while collapsing ages into four broad groups materially
changed at least one component in 3 of 12 panels.

Across the 12 custom APC panels, primary-window global period slopes ranged
from -0.291% per year to 0.038% per year. Alternative-window practical labels
agreed in all panels, and equal weighting changed the global period slope by at
most 0.002 percentage points per year. Opposing separately fitted age-specific
slopes occurred in 10 panels, indicating that aggregate trends can conceal age
heterogeneity.

# Interpretation

Increasing all-age quantities do not necessarily indicate worsening
age-standardized burden. Counts reflect population size and age composition in
addition to age-specific rates. The results may inform planning for potential
service volume and healthy life lost, but they do not measure realized service
use and do not establish causal effects of policies or health systems.

All derived changes, ratios, trends, breakpoints, contrasts, APC summaries, and
decomposition components are point estimates because posterior draws and
cross-estimate covariance were unavailable. Native GBD uncertainty intervals
apply only to the original endpoint estimates.

# Reproducibility

The analysis code, data provenance, data dictionary, model settings, validation
records, machine-readable tables, and generated figures are retained under
`analysis/`. The final analysis checks confirm complete annual
panels, official population inputs, valid uncertainty bounds, exact
decomposition closure, and consistent reconstruction of all-age quantities.
